rationale: Tests recognition of a quote with a price but effectively no scope, quantity, or diagnostic basis behind it.
quote_text:
Delton Maintenance Services

Quote reference: verbal site visit, kitchen area.

Water leak repair - plumbing work as required.
Materials extra at actual.

Charge: Rs. 8,500

Work to commence on receipt of advance. Balance on completion.
Contact: Delton Maintenance, 10am to 7pm.

should_identify: 'Plumbing work as required' is not a scope — nothing states what will actually be done.
'Materials extra at actual' means the Rs. 8,500 is not the final cost, and no cap or estimate is given.
No source of the leak, no inspection finding, and no measurement appear anywhere.
An advance is requested against undefined work.
should_preserve_uncertainty: Whether Rs. 8,500 is labour only, or labour plus some materials, is not stated.
The extent of the leak and what repairing it involves is entirely undetermined by this text.
must_not_invent: A likely cause of the leak, a pipe type, or a repair method. The quote supports none of these.
A price judgment on Rs. 8,500 — with no scope at all, there is nothing to judge it against even in principle.
semantic_expectations.notes: This case is the clearest instance of the allowed/forbidden price boundary: 'we cannot tell what this Rs. 8,500 buys' is the correct observation; 'this is high for a leak repair' is the forbidden one. Note the vendor is not accused of anything — thin quotes are common and often honest.
